District & Sessions Judge : New Delhi District :
 New Delhi
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
This appeal is directed against the order dated 25.11.2014 (hereinafter referred to as "Impugned Order") passed by Sh. Som Naidu, Ld. Adjudicating Officer/ADM (North), Govt. of NCT of Delhi whereby penalty of Rs. 40,000/ was imposed upon the appellant praying therein ; to set aside the impugned order.
FSAT Appeal No. 83/2014 page no. 1 of 6 Amit Aggarwal Vs. FSO 2.
The appeal was admitted.
The notice of the appeal was given to the respondent who has resisted the same.
The record of the Ld. Adjudicating Officer was requisitioned.
3. I have heard the rival contentions advanced on behalf of both the parties and have carefully perused the trial court record.

Shri Amit Aggarwal vs State Through Food Safety Officer on 8 September, 2015 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/64752698/
1 4.

entities.text: Amit Aggarwal vs State Through Food Safety Officer on 8 September, 2015 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Feeling aggrieved, the appellant has challenged the impugned order mainly on the following two grounds;
a) Ld. Adjudicating Officer/ADM has failed to appreciate that the 'date of manufacture' or 'best before date' or 'expiry date' is not required to be mentioned on the package having surface area of less than 30 sq. centimeters but these information shall be mentioned on the wholesale packages or multipiece packages, as the case may be.

b) The report of the public analyst has not been made or signed on the date on which the analysis was done, thus, the report in the instant petition also loses its evidentiary sanctity and as such,
impugned order deserves to be set aside.
5.

The case of the prosecution in brief is that on 30.05.2013 at about 4 PM Food Safety Officer Ms.
Usha Kiran went to the shop of Sh. Amit Aggarwal, FBO M/s Aggarwal Agency, Society, Bus Stand,
Bawana Road, Delhi 110039 and purchased the sample of Pan Masala after FSAT Appeal No.
83/2014 page no. 2 of 6 Amit Aggarwal Vs. FSO paying Rs. 1200/ as its cost.
Four sample packets were fastened, sealed and the signatures of FBO were obtained as per the prescribed procedure.
The panchnama in Form VA prepared and the signature of the Food Business Operator (FBO) was obtained as the token of its acknowledgment.
One sealed packet of the sample was sent to the food analyst, Delhi.

On testing, it was not found to be adulterated, however, it was stated to be misbranding because the same was not having batch number and nutritional information on the label of the packet and hence, the appellant violated the Regulations 2.2.2.9 of the Food Safety and Standard (Packaging and Labelling) Regulation, 2011 (hereinafter to be referred 'FSSRs (Packaging and Labelling).

entities.text: Food Safety and Standard (Packaging and Labelling) Regulation, 2011
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: Ld. Adjudicating officer did impose the penalty of Rs. 40,000/ on the report of Food Analyst.

6. First and foremost point raised by the Ld. Counsel for the appellant is that he is protected under the rules 2.6 of the FSSRs (Packaging and Labelling) which provides exemption from labeling requirements under 2.6.1 in sub clause (2).

On receipt of the notice, the appellant appeared and filed reply of the complaint before Ld. Adjudicating Officer mentioning therein that the counter part of the sample be summoned to calculate the surface area of the pouch of Pan Masala.

Accordingly the sample was produced before the Ld. Adjudicating Officer but he refused to open the said sealed packet containing small pouch to ascertain the surface area and as such appellant was deprived of his legal defence and the complaint was decided by imposing the penalty of Rs. 40,000/ without affording an opportunity to lead the defence evidence which is contrary to the FSAT Appeal No.
83/2014 page no. 3 of 6 Amit Aggarwal Vs. FSO principle of nature justice.
7.
Per contra, the learned Special PP has refuted the entire line of arguments while making submissions that the Food Inspector was within its power to lift the sample of Pan Masala.

He further stated that the date of manufacture or best before date or expiry date was required to be mentioned on the packets having surface area of even less than 30 sq. centimeter and as such it comes within the mischief of Section 16(1)(a) of Prevention of Food Adulteration Act (herein after referred to as "the Act").
Shri Amit Aggarwal vs State Through Food Safety Officer on 8 September, 2015 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/64752698/
2 8.

entities.text: Amit Aggarwal vs State Through Food Safety Officer
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Rule 2.6.1 (2) of the FSSRs (Packaging and Labelling) stipulates that the 'date of manufacture' or 'best before date' or 'expiry date' required to be mentioned on the package having surface are of less than 30 sq. centimeters but these information shall be given on the wholesale packages or multi piece packages, as the case may be.
Now the question arises as to whether the sampled pouch of Pan Masala was having surface area of less than 30 sq. centimeters or more.
There is no whisper from the the record with regard to the total surface area of the pouch of Pan Masala.
There is no iota of evidence on record either from the Prosecution or from the accused side to show the surface area of the pouch of Pan Masala.

Best course for the Ld. Adjudicating Officer was to direct the Prosecution to produce the pouch of Pan Masala in order to ascertain the surface area before arriving at the conclusion but he has failed to do so thus, a violation of principle of natural justice "Audi Alteram partem" i.e. no one should be condemned unheard.
FSAT Appeal No. 83/2014 page no. 4 of 6 Amit Aggarwal Vs. FSO 9.

His second line of argument is that the sample was taken on 30.05.2013 and the public analyst started the analysis on 03.06.2013 and completed the same on 08.06.2013 whereas he did sign the report on 10.06.2013 which apparently indicates the delay in signing the report of the public analyst and then the report would certainly lose the evidentiary value.

To support his contention, he placed reliance upon the judgment as reported Delhi Administration Vs. Amar Chand, 2012 (3) JCC 1930 (DHC) wherein, the Lordship was pleased to make the following observations: Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954 Public Analyst Report Sample was taken on 10.11.2005 and the Public Analyst completed the analysis on 17.11.2005 whereas he signed his report on 29.01.2005Delay in signing the report by the Public Analyst Reliance cannot be placed upon the report of the Public Analysis who analyzed the sample on 17.11.2005 and finalized by signing it on 29.11.2005.
9.

entities.text: Delhi Administration Vs. Amar Chand, 2012 (3) JCC 1930 (DHC)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: If the facts of the instant case are examined in the light of aforesaid observations, it appears that the report of the public analyst was not made at the same time when sample was analyzed and the same was made later on, then on the basis of the notes of the analyst made at the time of analysis will cease to have an evidentiary value.

10. On the basis of reappreciation of the material including FSAT Appeal No. 83/2014 page no. 5 of 6 Amit Aggarwal Vs. FSO the evidence from the trial court record, I am of the considered view that the court of Ld. Adjudicating Officer fell into an error and failed to appreciate the attended circumstances with the adduced material including the documents such as Public Analyst report in a proper legal perspective and in this regard, the order of the Ld. Adjudicating Officer is vitiated with error of law, impropriety and misappreciation of the material and in this context, I feel every justification to interfere in the impugned order given by the court below.

Thus, the impugned order dated 25.11.2014 is set aside by accepting the appeal and remand the case to the Ld. Adjudicating Officer/ADM (North), Govt. of NCT of Delhi to decide the case afresh after hearing both the parties.
Both the parties are directed to appear before the concerned court on 18.09.2015.
Appeal file be consigned to the record room.
TCR be sent back along with the copy of this judgment.
